newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Petkim workers halt protest.
newsitem.headline: Turk Petkim workers halt protest.

text.p: Around 3,500 workers at Turkey's largely state-owned petrochemicals firm Petrokimya Holding A.S. (Petkim) who began protests on Tuesday morning, temporarily halted their action on Thursday.

Mustafa Oztaskin, the representative of Petrol-Is petroleum workers' union, said this did not mean an end to their demands for higher wages following a 101 percent increase in the minimum wage in August.

"As a result of our meetings with the management of Petkim, we have temporarily halted our action. During this time we want our rights recognised, otherwise we will start tougher actions," Oztaskin told Reuters.
During the protest at Petkim's Aliaga plant near the western port city of Izmir, the workers staged sit-ins and stopped goods despatches, but production was allowed to continue.

Petrol-Is says an article in the labour contract requires wages for new employees to be raised in tandem with the rise in the minimum wage and the whole pay scale must be adjusted upwards accordingly.
Petkim general manager Mehmet Yilmaz has said he supports the union demands and is talking to the government about them.
